title: Tony Fadell joins Smartex as chair as it launches AI fabric checks for H&M
excerpt: Tony Fadell is now chair of Smartex, whose AI cameras check fabric for defects. H&M is a launch customer, Fortune reports.
content_html:
Tony Fadell, who helped create the iPod and iPhone, has become chair of Smartex, a startup that uses AI to check fabric for defects, Fortune reported. H&M, an investor in Smartex, is one of the first customers for its new products.

Smartex is launching two products. Smartex Inspect is a camera system that attaches to existing textile machines and checks the material as it moves past. Smartex IQ turns the data from those systems into supply chain insights.

The company says its system works three times faster than a human inspector, according to Fortune. In most textile mills, workers still check fabric by eye, often against a handful of colour swatches.

“There’s no Pantone color for quality inspection,” Fadell told Fortune.

Brands often order about 5% more fabric than they need to cover for defects, chief executive Max Easton told Fortune. He estimated that Smartex could save H&M about $100m a year by cutting that waste. TNW has not verified the estimate.

To train its system, Smartex uses a library of 50 billion fabric images. The system has to adjust for lighting, speed and small colour changes, and match each client’s standards.

Fadell has invested about $10m in Smartex, according to Fortune. His fund, Build Collective, co-led a $24.7m Series A in 2022 with Lightspeed Venture Partners. H&M Group also took part.

Smartex was founded in Porto in 2018. It has about 65 employees and has installed 800 of its older systems in 10 countries, Fortune reported.
